check.improved:
TCP uses a three-way handshake to establish a connection. First, the client sends a SYN packet to the server [p. 1]. Then, the server responds with a SYN-ACK packet [p. 1]. Finally, the client sends an ACK packet to confirm the connection [p. 1]. This sequence ensures that both the client and server are ready to send data [p. 1]. The handshake is crucial for ensuring reliable communication [p. 1]. Here is a simple example of a TCP three-way handshake in Python:

```python
import socket

# Server setup
server_socket = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
server_socket.bind(('localhost', 12345))
server_socket.listen(5)

# Client setup
client_socket = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
client_socket.connect(('localhost', 12345))

# Three-way handshake
client_socket.send(b'SYN')
server_socket.send(b'SYN-ACK')
client_socket.send(b'ACK')

# Connection established
client_socket.close()
server_socket.close()
```

This example demonstrates the SYN, SYN-ACK, and ACK packets exchanged during the handshake. [p. 1]
